title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 25
paragraphs: So the barbarians were paying honor in their own fashion to the slain Masistios. The Greeks, however, having sustained the cavalry's attack and, having sustained it, having driven them back, were much more encouraged. First they placed the dead body in a cart and conveyed it along their ranks — and the body was a sight worth seeing for its size and beauty, so that the men even left their places in ranks and went one after another to gaze upon Masistios. After this they resolved to come further down toward Plataea, for the Plataean region was seen to be far more convenient for them to camp in than Erythrai — both for other reasons and because it is better watered. To this region, then, and to the spring Gargaphia which is there, they resolved they must go and encamp in their separate positions. So they took up their arms and went along the lower slopes of Kithairon past Hysiai to the Plataean land; and on arrival they posted themselves by nations near the spring Gargaphia and the sacred precinct of the hero Androcrates, over low hills and level ground.
